articles.title: Food aid cut for half a million Palestinians in Gaza, as fatal Israeli strikes continue
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: At least eight Palestinians, including four children, were killed in Israeli assaults in different parts of the Gaza Strip over the last two days. On Monday, October 19, Israeli forces launched drone strikes on north-central Gaza City and the southern city of Khan Younis, killing a Palestinian man and two children. One day earlier, five Palestinians were killed and several others were injured in Israeli shelling and gunfire across the besieged enclave. This includes two children, who were shot dead by Israeli soldiers in separate attacks. One of the slain children was identified as 13-year-old Tamer Soboh , who was killed in the northern city of Beit Lahia; the other was Misk al-Dalu , who died after Israeli troops opened fire at tents sheltering displaced people in al-Maghazi refugee camp

articles.title: Curfews imposed in French cities as rebellion against austerity grows nationwide
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Mass mobilizations against austerity policies and their effects are not winding down in France. On Saturday, October 17 , roughly 800,000 people joined protests across more than 1,700 assembly points, according to union figures – amplifying demands tabled over a month of student protests and demanding urgent action on the cost of living crisis. In the aftermath of the protests, the government expanded local authorities’ powers to introduce curfews. This led to overnight movement limitation orders introduced in several cities, including central parts of Paris, Lille, Lyon, and Nice. Many of the curfews target young people in particular, reflecting institutional concern about the success of their recent mobilizations. articles.title: Capitalism, Peasants, Family Farms: A Bibliographical Essay
articles.author: Panagiotis Sotiris
articles.content_excerpt: By the end of 2015 some forty percent or more of China’s rural workforce was thought to consist of roughly 250 million peasant migrants known as mingong, a cross between nongmin (peasant) and gongren (worker). articles.title: Students across the US South demand justice for Nolan Wells
articles.author: Devin B. Martinez
articles.content_excerpt: Calls for justice and for the reopening of Nolan Wells’ case are mounting after a grand jury declined to bring criminal charges, despite the question of Wells’ cause of death remaining unanswered. Wells, a young Black student at Southwest Mississippi Community College, went on a boating trip on July 4 to Horn Island, just off the coast of Mississippi, with several white friends. He never returned. His friends, who returned to the mainland with Wells’ cell phone but without him, claimed he chose to stay behind. Wells’ body was found in the water near Horn Island two days later. articles.title: French Gov’t Cracks Down on Mass Protests over Cost of Living, Education Cuts; 2,400+ Arrested
articles.content_excerpt: Hundreds of thousands of protesters marched in over 140 cities across France on Saturday, demanding relief from the high cost of living, more funding for public services and improvements to deteriorating schools, among other grievances. The demonstrations were the latest — and largest — in a series of protests that began in September with high schooler-led demonstrations against overcrowded classrooms and crumbling school infrastructure. Some cities saw property destruction, arson and theft on Saturday, with city halls and other symbols of the state coming under attack. articles.title: Masked Israeli Settlers Nearly Kill Washington Post Journalist as Attacks on Palestinians Escalate
articles.content_excerpt: Israeli settlers backed by IDF soldiers brutally assaulted Palestinian olive farmers in the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, on Friday. Witnesses say dozens of masked Israeli settlers armed with clubs, sticks, slingshots and guns hurled rocks at Palestinian farmers, set olive trees ablaze and drove people from their fields. Veteran Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, a 64-year-old American, was documenting the attack when settlers began beating her. She suffered stab wounds, a broken rib, four broken vertebrae and a severe hand injury. Levine was wearing a clearly marked press vest and a helmet at the time of the attack. articles.title: Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa: Prominent Anti-Corruption Lawyer in Guatemala Assassinated
articles.content_excerpt: The prominent Guatemalan anti-corruption lawyer Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa was fatally shot along with another man on Saturday at a sports center in Guatemala City. articles.title: Culture and the Moment
articles.author: Sage Crump
articles.content_excerpt: Artists and cultural workers are an integral part of all revolutionary movements across geography and time. From Chinese puppetry, to the harmonies of Sweet Honey in the Rock, to the Místicas of the Landless Workers Movement (MST) in Brazil, culture has added to the canon of what resistance can look like. Living in a time of authoritarianism and proto-fascism means culture has been hijacked. Source
